note: 25 Nov 2026 (the owner): Part 4 discusses, expresses, supports and maintains a view. Four questions per topic, Maya with both candidates. Tomás: React (stance), View (about people), Support (a reason OR an example), Concede, Maintain. Beatriz, the safe answer: React, View, Reason, (So / That's why…). After each answer the partner joins in by name; twice per topic the view is challenged and held. Chunks varied: never twice in a topic.

Maintaining it: But at the end of the day,…
That's true, but I still think…
I see what you mean, but…
Joining in (by name): I don't really agree with Tomás.

stages.t: Definitely.
As far as I'm concerned, most teenagers spend too much time on their phones.
The main reason is that people check them without thinking.
It's true that phones are useful for school.
But overall, we use them far too much.
I agree with Tomás.
Also, people sleep less because of their phones.

questions.question: Do you think young people spend too much time on their phones?

stages.t: Hmm, it's hard to say.
I think social media is good for friendships,
because you can talk to your friends every day.
That's why I use it a lot.
I see Beatriz's point, but I'm not sure.
For me, a real friendship needs time together.
Maybe, but I still think it helps.

questions.question: Is social media good or bad for friendships?

stages.t: That's a tricky one.
Personally, I think schools should ban phones in class.
For example, when our school did it, people talked more at break.
Of course, phones can be useful in an emergency.
Even so, the ban is a good idea.
I'm afraid I disagree with Tomás.
Students need their phones to talk to their parents.
I understand, but they can use the school phone.

questions.question: Should schools ban mobile phones?

stages.t: Not really.
In my opinion, robots will do some jobs, but not most of them,
since people still need other people.
Beatriz is right.
What's more, robots will create new jobs too.

questions.question: Will robots do most jobs in the future?

stages.t: Good question.
From my point of view, a good teacher is patient.
For instance, my maths teacher never makes us feel stupid.
Admittedly, being strict is important too.
But at the end of the day, patience matters most.
Like Tomás said, patience is important.
On top of that, a good teacher makes lessons fun.

questions.question: What makes someone a good teacher?

stages.t: Not really.
For me, learning in a classroom is better,
because you can ask the teacher questions.
That's why I prefer school.
I partly agree with Beatriz.
The way I see it, online learning is great for revision.
Maybe, but I still prefer a real teacher.

questions.question: Is online learning as good as learning in a classroom?

stages.t: Absolutely.
I strongly believe students should have less homework.
The reason is that we're already tired after school.
It's true that some homework helps you practise.
All the same, two hours every night is too much.
I don't really agree with Tomás.
Without homework, many students would forget everything.
I see what you mean, but less homework doesn't mean no homework.

questions.question: Should students have less homework?

stages.t: Yes, definitely.
I believe everyone should learn to cook at school,
as it's useful for the rest of your life.
I couldn't agree more with Beatriz.
Another thing is that people would eat more healthily.

questions.question: Should everyone learn to cook at school?

stages.t: It depends.
In my opinion, a small job at the weekend is a good idea,
since it teaches you to be responsible.
Of course, school should always come first.
Even so, a few hours a week can't hurt.
I agree with Tomás about school.
Also, you learn the value of money.

questions.question: Should teenagers have part-time jobs?

stages.t: That's easy.
I'd say enjoying your job is more important,
because you work every day.
So money isn't everything.
Hmm, I'm not so sure, Beatriz.
If you ask me, money matters too, because life is expensive.
That's true, but I still think happiness comes first.

questions.question: Is it more important to enjoy your job or to earn a lot of money?

stages.t: Definitely.
I'm convinced that schools should teach how to manage money.
Take my cousin, for example: she spent her first salary in a week!
Admittedly, parents can teach it at home.
But not every family talks about money, so schools should do it.
I'm afraid I disagree.
School already has too many subjects.
I understand, but this subject is more useful than most.

questions.question: Should young people learn how to manage money at school?

stages.t: Yes, I think so.
Personally, I believe people work too much these days,
because many parents get home very late.
Beatriz has a point.
What's more, people answer work emails at home.

questions.question: Do you think people work too much these days?

stages.t: Not really.
The way I see it, most people don't exercise enough.
The main reason is that we sit down all day, at school or at work.
It's true that more people go to the gym now.
But overall, we move much less than in the past.
I agree with Tomás.
On top of that, people drive everywhere, even for short trips.

questions.question: Do you think people exercise enough these days?

stages.t: Good question.
I think fast food is popular
because it's cheap and quick.
That's why teenagers love it.
Beatriz is right about the price, but
for me, advertising is the real reason.
Maybe, but I still think the price matters most.

questions.question: Why is fast food so popular?

stages.t: Absolutely.
From my point of view, sport should be compulsory at school.
For example, many teenagers never do any exercise outside school.
Of course, not everyone enjoys team sports.
Even so, everyone needs to move.
I'm not so sure, Tomás.
Some students hate PE, and they feel embarrassed.
I understand, but schools can offer different sports, like dance or swimming.

questions.question: Should sport be compulsory at school?

stages.t: Yes, definitely.
In my view, footballers are paid too much,
since nurses and teachers earn much less.
I couldn't agree more.
Another thing is that young fans think money is everything.

questions.question: Are professional footballers paid too much?

stages.t: Quite a lot, actually.
I strongly believe young people can make a difference.
For instance, they can recycle and take the bus.
Admittedly, governments have to do the most.
All the same, small changes add up.
Like Tomás said, small things matter.
Also, young people can teach their parents.

questions.question: What can young people do to help the environment?

stages.t: Yes, I think so.
For me, fast fashion is a big problem,
because people throw away clothes very quickly.
So we should buy less.
I partly agree with Beatriz.
But to be honest, cheap clothes help families with less money.
That's true, but I still think we buy too much.

questions.question: Is fast fashion a problem we should care about?

stages.t: Definitely.
As far as I'm concerned, buses should be free for teenagers.
The reason is that fewer parents would drive their children to school.
It's true that it would cost a lot of money.
But at the end of the day, it's good for the planet.
I don't really agree, Tomás.
The buses here are often late, so free buses won't change anything.
I see what you mean, but more passengers would mean better buses.

questions.question: Should public transport be free for teenagers?

stages.t: It's hard to say.
I'd say tourism is good for islands like Madeira,
as many people work in hotels and restaurants.
Beatriz is right about the jobs.
However, too many tourists can damage nature, like on the levadas.

questions.question: Is tourism good or bad for places like islands?

stages.t: A few close ones, definitely.
In my opinion, a few real friends are better than lots of friends,
since you can trust them when something goes wrong.
Of course, having lots of friends is fun.
Even so, close friends matter more.
I agree with Tomás.
What's more, close friends know you really well.

questions.question: Is it better to have lots of friends or a few close ones?

stages.t: Not always.
I believe teenagers and parents don't always understand each other,
because they grew up in a different world.
That's why we argue sometimes.
I see Beatriz's point, but it depends on the family.
In many families, parents and teenagers talk about everything.
Maybe, but I still think it's difficult.

questions.question: Do teenagers and parents understand each other?

stages.t: Absolutely not.
The way I see it, video games aren't a waste of time.
For example, many games teach you to work in a team.
Admittedly, some people play for too many hours.
But overall, games can be really useful.
I'm afraid I disagree with Tomás.
Most teenagers play games instead of doing homework.
I understand, but that's a problem of time, not of games.

questions.question: Are video games a waste of time?

stages.t: Hmm, good question.
For me, growing up in a small town is better,
because it's safer and quieter.
Beatriz has a point.
On top of that, in a small town everybody knows you.

questions.question: Is it better to grow up in a city or a small town?
